_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Guinea-Bissau covering Kaabu Empire, Portuguese Guinea, Amílcar Cabral's PAIGC liberation war, coups, and narco-state dynamics.

ethnic_groups.name: Balanta
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; southern Guinea-Bissau; rice farmers; stateless society tradition; majority animist; dominated PAIGC liberation army

ethnic_groups.name: Fula/Fulani (Fula/Fulbe)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern and eastern regions; Gabú; Fouta Djallon links; predominantly Muslim; pastoralist heritage; commercial and political influence

ethnic_groups.name: Manjaco (Manjak)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern coastal; Cacheu region; rice cultivation; cross-border with Senegal (Casamance)

ethnic_groups.name: Mandinka (Mandinga)
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Guinea-Bissau; Gabú region; remnants of Kaabu Empire; Muslim; Mande people; strong Mali Empire heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Papel (Pepel)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bissau and Biombo region; coastal agriculturalists; rice growers

ethnic_groups.name: Bijagó (Bissagos Islanders)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bijagós Archipelago; distinct maritime culture; matrilineal; historically resisted Portuguese until 20th century

ethnic_groups.name: Mancanha
ethnic_groups.notes: Central coastal; related to Papel and Manjaco

ethnic_groups.name: Beafada
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Guinea-Bissau; related to Tenda group

ethnic_groups.name: Felupe/Jola
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern border; rice farmers; Casamance cultural area

ethnic_groups.name: Nalu
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern coastal; related to Guinea groups

ethnic_groups.name: Other (including Cape Verdean, Lebanese, Portuguese)
ethnic_groups.notes: Cape Verdean Creoles influential; Lebanese traders; small Portuguese community

natural_resources.notes: Cashew nuts dominant export (6th globally, 85% of export earnings); fishing (rich waters, EU fishing agreements); Bijagós Archipelago UNESCO Biosphere Reserve; offshore oil potential (disputed with Senegal, now joint development); timber; largely agrarian economy

military.notes: Chronically unstable military—4 successful coups since independence (1980, 1999, 2003, 2012); military-narco nexus (cocaine transit from Latin America to Europe, 'Africa's first narco-state'); ECOWAS ECOMIB stabilization force; February 2022 coup attempt failed

debt_aid.notes: Heavily aid-dependent; HIPC debt relief; cashew monoculture vulnerability; narco-economy (cocaine transit estimated worth more than GDP); political instability deters investment

education.notes: Portuguese-language instruction; Kriol (creole) spoken widely; very low educational attainment; Amílcar Cabral's education legacy (revolutionary schools in liberated zones); Catholic mission schools significant; gender gap severe

diaspora_migration.notes: Portuguese connection primary migration route; Lusophone diaspora networks; Bijagós islanders relatively isolated; narcotics-related migration patterns; seasonal workers in Senegal/Gambia

digital_economy.notes: Minimal digital infrastructure; Orange Bissau primary telecom; among lowest internet penetration in Africa; no meaningful tech ecosystem; power supply unreliable; AfricaConnect improving backbone

current_leader.name: Umaro Sissoco Embaló
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Former general and PM; disputed 2019 election; MADEM-G15 party; survived attempted coup 2022

former_leaders.name: Luís Cabral
former_leaders.notes: Half-brother of Amílcar Cabral; first president; Cape Verdean; overthrown by Vieira

former_leaders.name: João Bernardo 'Nino' Vieira
former_leaders.notes: Led 1980 coup; civil war 1998–1999; returned via 2005 election; assassinated March 2009 in retaliation for military chief killing

former_leaders.name: Kumba Ialá
former_leaders.notes: First elected post-civil war president; deposed by military; died 2014

former_leaders.name: José Mário Vaz
former_leaders.notes: First president to complete full term without coup or assassination; PAIGC

910.name: Prehistoric Guinea-Bissau
910.description: Early settlement of the Bijagós archipelago and coastal mainland; rice cultivation origins.

sub_clusters.name: Bijagós Archipelago Early Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Settlement of the Bijagós Islands; maritime adaptation; early fishing communities.

sub_clusters.name: Coastal Rice Cultivation Origins
sub_clusters.description: Indigenous African rice (Oryza glaberrima) cultivation in coastal wetlands; Balanta paddy systems.

920.name: Kaabu Empire
920.description: Mandinka Kaabu successor state of Mali Empire; powerful kingdom dominating Guinea-Bissau and southern Senegal.

sub_clusters.name: Foundation as Mali Province
sub_clusters.description: Kaabu established as westernmost province of Mali Empire; Mandinka nyanthio warrior aristocracy.

sub_clusters.name: Independent Kaabu Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Kaabu becomes independent after Mali decline; controls trade routes; capital at Kansala.

sub_clusters.name: Battle of Kansala
sub_clusters.description: Fouta Djallon Fulbe army destroys Kansala; end of Kaabu Empire; last Mandinka resistance.

920.name: Bijagós Maritime Culture
920.description: Bijagó people of the archipelago; seafaring warriors; matrilineal society; resistance to colonialism.

sub_clusters.name: Bijagós Warrior Society
sub_clusters.description: Maritime raiding; age-grade initiation; matrilineal inheritance; sacred islands.

930.name: Portuguese Contact and Slave Trade
930.description: Portuguese exploration; Cacheu and Bissau trading posts; slave trade; lançados and grumetes.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Exploration
sub_clusters.description: Nuno Tristão explores coast 1446; Cacheu established; trade in wax, hides, and slaves.

sub_clusters.name: Cacheu and Bissau Slave Trade
sub_clusters.description: Cacheu becomes major slave port; Bissau fortress 1687; lançados (Portuguese-African traders).

sub_clusters.name: Lançados and Creole Society
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese-African intermediaries; Kriol language formation; Creole Catholic communities.

940.name: Colonial Portuguese Guinea
940.description: Colony formally established; pacification campaigns; forced labour; groundnut economy; minimal development.

sub_clusters.name: Pacification Campaigns
sub_clusters.description: Colony proclaimed 1879; decades of resistance; Bijagós not subdued until 1936.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Economy and Forced Labour
sub_clusters.description: Groundnut monoculture; forced labour; extreme underdevelopment; poorest Portuguese colony.

sub_clusters.name: Pidjiguiti Dock Strike and Massacre
sub_clusters.description: Dock workers strike in Bissau; Portuguese massacre of strikers; radicalises independence movement.

950.name: PAIGC Liberation War
950.description: Amílcar Cabral founds PAIGC; guerrilla war; liberated zones; Cabral assassination; independence.

sub_clusters.name: PAIGC Founded
sub_clusters.description: Amílcar Cabral founds PAIGC 1956 in Bissau; political mobilisation; armed struggle begins 1963.

sub_clusters.name: Liberation War
sub_clusters.description: PAIGC controls 2/3 of territory by 1968; 'People's Stores'; liberated zone governance.

sub_clusters.name: Assassination of Amílcar Cabral
sub_clusters.description: Cabral assassinated in Conakry January 1973; suspected Portuguese PIDE involvement.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Guinea-Bissau
sub_clusters.description: Unilateral declaration September 1973; recognised after Portuguese Carnation Revolution 1974.

960.name: Postcolonial Instability
960.description: Luís Cabral; Nino Vieira coup; single-party state; 1998-1999 civil war.

sub_clusters.name: Luís Cabral Era
sub_clusters.description: Luís Cabral president; Guinea-Bissau–Cabo Verde unity plan; economic difficulties.

sub_clusters.name: Nino Vieira Coup and Rule
sub_clusters.description: João Bernardo 'Nino' Vieira coup 1980; single-party then multiparty rule; growing instability.

sub_clusters.name: 1998-1999 Civil War
sub_clusters.description: Ansumane Mané rebellion; Senegalese and Guinean intervention; Vieira ousted.

960.name: Narco-State Crisis and Chronic Instability
960.description: Cocaine trafficking hub; assassinations; serial coups; Embaló presidency.

sub_clusters.name: Vieira Return and Assassination
sub_clusters.description: Vieira returns as president 2005; assassinated March 2009 hours after army chief killed.

sub_clusters.name: Cocaine Trafficking Hub
sub_clusters.description: Guinea-Bissau becomes Latin American cocaine transhipment point to Europe; military complicity.

sub_clusters.name: Embaló Presidency and 2022 Coup Attempt
sub_clusters.description: Umaro Sissoco Embaló elected 2019; disputed; February 2022 coup attempt; dissolved parliament 2023.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
